```{=html}
<section class="band band-green">
  <div class="band-narrow">

    <p class="eyebrow">Our Finger Lakes</p>

    <h2 class="section-title">Things to Do</h2>

    <p class="date-place" style="text-transform:none; letter-spacing:0.04em; font-size:1rem">
      We have spent years eating, hiking, and drinking our way around this place, and June is
      the best month to be here. Make a weekend of it &mdash; here is where we would send you.
    </p>

  </div>
</section>

<section class="band band-cream">
  <div class="band-inner">

    <p class="eyebrow" style="text-align:center">Cayuga, Seneca &amp; Keuka</p>

    <h2 class="section-title" style="text-align:center">Wineries &amp; Cider</h2>

    <div class="feature">
      <div class="feature-body">
        <div class="place">Ovid &nbsp;·&nbsp; Cayuga Lake</div>
        <h3>Hosmer Winery</h3>
        <p>Start here. The Riesling and Cabernet Franc genuinely set the bar on this lake, and the
        vineyards are some of the oldest on Cayuga &mdash; planted more than fifty years ago.</p>
        <p class="feature-note">Riley worked here, so we are hopelessly biased.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="feature-pattern"></div>
    </div>

    <div class="listing">

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Six Eighty Cellars</h4>
        <div class="place">Ovid &nbsp;·&nbsp; Cayuga Lake</div>
        <p>The most interesting tasting in the region. Small-batch wines aged in clay, concrete, and terracotta, on a steep slope with a huge view down the lake. Go if you want something unexpected.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Hermann J. Wiemer</h4>
        <div class="place">Dundee &nbsp;·&nbsp; Seneca Lake</div>
        <p>The benchmark for Finger Lakes Riesling, full stop. Worth crossing over to Seneca for. Their dry Riesling is on the wine list at our reception.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Dr. Konstantin Frank</h4>
        <div class="place">Hammondsport &nbsp;·&nbsp; Keuka Lake</div>
        <p>The furthest drive of the bunch and the one with the most history &mdash; the winery that proved vinifera could grow here at all. Pair it with a day around Keuka if you have the time.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Finger Lakes Cider House</h4>
        <div class="place">Interlaken &nbsp;·&nbsp; Route 89</div>
        <p>Our favorite low-key afternoon. Excellent dry cider, a food menu sourced from the neighboring farms and their own organic land, and a porch looking out over the orchard.</p>
      </div>

    </div>

  </div>
</section>

<section class="band band-shells">
  <div class="band-narrow">

    <div class="panel-card">

      <p class="eyebrow">Gorges, obviously</p>

      <h2 class="section-title">Get Outside</h2>

      <p style="line-height:1.8">
        Ithaca is gorges. We are contractually obligated to say it, and it is also true &mdash;
        there are waterfalls within fifteen minutes of town in nearly every direction.
      </p>

      <ul style="line-height:2.1; padding-left:1.2rem">
        <li><strong>Taughannock Falls</strong> &mdash; a 215-foot plunge, taller than Niagara, and where we are having the Friday welcome party. The gorge trail to the base is flat, shaded, and stroller-friendly; the rim trail is the better view.</li>
        <li><strong>Watkins Glen State Park</strong> &mdash; the showstopper. Nineteen waterfalls along a stone gorge trail with tunnels and bridges. Closest to the venue, and the busiest, so go early.</li>
        <li><strong>Robert H. Treman</strong> &mdash; our pick for a hot day. You can swim at the base of a waterfall in the lower park.</li>
        <li><strong>Buttermilk Falls</strong> &mdash; right in town, quick, and beautiful. Good if you only have an hour.</li>
      </ul>

      <p style="line-height:1.8; margin-bottom:0">
        Wear real shoes &mdash; the gorge trails are wet stone and they stay slick even in June.
      </p>

    </div>

  </div>
</section>

<section class="band band-cream">
  <div class="band-inner">

    <p class="eyebrow" style="text-align:center">Where we actually eat</p>

    <h2 class="section-title" style="text-align:center">Food, Coffee &amp; Ice Cream</h2>

    <div class="listing">

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Sweet Melissa's</h4>
        <div class="place">Ithaca &amp; Trumansburg</div>
        <p>The ice cream institution. Homemade hard ice cream and a serious vegan lineup. There is a shop on West Seneca in Ithaca and one in Trumansburg.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Spotted Duck Creamery</h4>
        <div class="place">Penn Yan</div>
        <p>Frozen custard made with duck egg yolks instead of chicken &mdash; denser and richer than anything you have had. It is a drive and it is worth it. Our sentimental favorite.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Main Street Market</h4>
        <div class="place">Trumansburg</div>
        <p>Sandwiches, salads, local groceries, Wide Awake Bakery bread, and beer and cider on tap. The best quick lunch on the way to or from the lake.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Finger Lakes Cider House</h4>
        <div class="place">Interlaken</div>
        <p>Worth listing twice. The food menu is as good a reason to go as the cider &mdash; everything comes off neighboring farms.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Gimme! Coffee</h4>
        <div class="place">Ithaca</div>
        <p>The original Ithaca roaster and still the one we go to most.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Press Bay Alley</h4>
        <div class="place">Ithaca</div>
        <p>Coffee plus a cluster of tiny shops in a converted alley off West State. A nice half hour on a Saturday morning.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Forty Weight Coffee Roasters</h4>
        <div class="place">Ithaca</div>
        <p>Rounding out the three. You genuinely cannot get a bad cup of coffee in this town.</p>
      </div>

    </div>


    <p class="eyebrow" style="text-align:center">Bring home something good</p>

    <h2 class="section-title" style="text-align:center">Shops</h2>

    <div class="listing">

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Home Green Home</h4>
        <div class="place">Ithaca Commons</div>
        <p>Sustainable home goods, linens, and gifts. Where a fair amount of our own apartment came from.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Petrune</h4>
        <div class="place">Ithaca Commons</div>
        <p>Beautifully curated vintage clothing. Worth a browse even if you are not buying.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Handwork</h4>
        <div class="place">Ithaca Commons</div>
        <p>A craft cooperative &mdash; pottery, jewelry, and textiles made by local artists who take turns staffing the shop.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="spot">
        <h4>Sundries</h4>
        <div class="place">Trumansburg</div>
        <p>A small, very well-edited general store. The good version of a gift shop.</p>
      </div>

    </div>

  </div>
</section>

<section class="band band-green">
  <div class="band-inner">

    <p class="eyebrow" style="text-align:center">For the little ones</p>

    <h2 class="section-title" style="text-align:center">With Kids</h2>

    <div class="kid-list">
      <p><strong>Sciencenter</strong> &mdash; a hands-on science museum built for kids, with an outdoor play area.</p>
      <p><strong>Ithaca Children's Garden</strong> &mdash; three acres of gardens designed to be climbed on and dug in.</p>
      <p><strong>Museum of the Earth</strong> &mdash; fossils, a full whale skeleton, and a very good rainy-day option.</p>
      <p><strong>Ithaca Farmers Market</strong> &mdash; Saturday and Sunday mornings on the water at Steamboat Landing. Food stalls, music, and room to run around. Our favorite thing to do in this town.</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</section>

<section class="band script-banner">
  <div class="plaque">
    <p>Ithaca is gorges, and we will not apologise for saying so.</p>
  </div>
</section>
```
